ex: Enter the promo code at checkout to get a discount.
This promo code gives you 20% off your order.
Sorry, this promo code expired yesterday.
I got a promo code by email from the store.
He jumped high and made a slam dunk.
The crowd cheered loudly after his slam dunk.
She practiced her slam dunk every day after school.
Can you do a slam dunk on this basket?
slam dunk.note: Also used informally for a sure success.

ex: Ha-ha, that's the funniest joke I've heard today!
"Ha-ha, very funny," she said with a smile.
He read my message and wrote back, "Ha-ha."
Ha-ha, I can't believe you really did that!
Religious fundamentalists protested outside the theater.
He became a fundamentalist after joining a strict church.
Fundamentalists believe every word of their holy book.
The new leader is a fundamentalist who hates any change.

ha-ha-ha.note: Used mostly in writing to show laughter.

ex: The choir sang the whole song a cappella.
Our school group sings a cappella, without any instruments.
Can you sing this song a cappella for us?
It is hard to sing a cappella and stay in tune.
The doctor answered anti-vax claims on her blog.
Anti-vax posts spread fast on social media.
My neighbor believes many anti-vax stories from the internet.
The school talks to parents about anti-vax myths.
anti-vax.note: Informal; usually an adjective (anti-vax posts). A person is an "anti-vaxxer."

ex: Let's split the restaurant bill fifty-fifty this time.
My brother and I pay the rent fifty-fifty.
We shared the cost of the trip fifty-fifty.
Can we divide the housework fifty-fifty, please?
fifty-fifty.note: Informal. Also an adjective: "a fifty-fifty chance."

ex: She was treated for pre-eclampsia during her pregnancy.
Pre-eclampsia can cause very high blood pressure in pregnant women.
Doctors check every pregnant woman for signs of pre-eclampsia.
Her baby was born early because of pre-eclampsia.

ex-president.note: "Former president" is more common in news and formal English.

duty-free.note: Often used as an adjective too: duty-free shop, duty-free goods.

ex: Fans love learning the lore of this video game.
The show has deep lore about its fantasy world.
He knows all the lore of the series by heart.
Can you explain the lore of this game to me?
lore.note: Uncountable. Also means old stories and beliefs: "local lore."

ballast.note: Uncountable: some ballast, a lot of ballast (not "a ballast").

ex: Our husky has bright blue eyes and thick fur.
Huskies love cold weather and lots of snow.
A team of huskies pulled the sled across the ice.
Our husky needs a long walk every day.
husky.note: Also an adjective: a "husky" voice is low and rough.

ex: A neutrino can pass right through the whole Earth.
Scientists built a huge detector to find neutrinos.
Neutrinos have almost no mass and no charge.
The sun sends out billions of neutrinos every second.

reset.note: Most often "reset" is a verb: "Reset your password here."

koi.note: Plural is "koi," the same as the singular.

ex: Piranhas have very sharp teeth and strong jaws.
Don't swim in rivers where piranhas live.
We saw some piranhas at the city aquarium.
A piranha bit the fisherman's finger on the boat.
He tries to act macho in front of the girls.
Real macho guys never ask for directions, he joked.
She is tired of macho men at the gym.
The film makes fun of macho heroes and their big guns.
macho.note: Informal; usually an adjective in English: "a macho man."

digest.note: Most often "digest" is a verb: "Food takes hours to digest."

tact.note: Uncountable: show tact, a lot of tact (not "a tact").

genesis.note: Most often "Genesis" is the first book of the Bible. As "origin," the word is formal.

ex: In Irish stories, a banshee cries before someone dies.
She screamed like a banshee when she saw the spider.
The kids were yelling like banshees in the backyard.
The book is about a banshee in an old house.
Write your initials at the bottom of each page.
His initials are on the front of his bag.
Please sign here with your initials, not your full name.
What do the initials on this ring mean?
initial.note: Most often "initial" is an adjective meaning first: "the initial plan."

ex: One byte is made up of eight bits.
This small text file is only a few bytes.
Each letter in this text uses one byte.
Computer memory is measured in bytes.
The lander touched down safely on the surface of Mars.
The lander sent the first photos back to Earth.
Engineers tested the lunar lander before the mission.
The lander carried a small robot to the moon.

express.note: Most often "express" is a verb: "Express your ideas clearly."

ex: Chocolate is my kryptonite, so I never buy it.
In the comics, kryptonite makes the hero weak.
Early mornings are my kryptonite; I always feel tired.
Sweets are kryptonite for my diet.
kryptonite.note: Often means a weakness: "Pizza is my kryptonite."

ex: We saw a mother orangutan and her baby at the zoo.
Orangutans live in the rain forests of Southeast Asia.
The orangutan slowly ate a banana in the tree.
Baby orangutans stay with their mothers for years.
I made cheese ravioli for dinner tonight.
This ravioli has spinach and cheese inside.
The kids love ravioli with tomato sauce.
Boil the ravioli for about four minutes.
ravioli.note: Uncountable: some ravioli, a plate of ravioli.

ex: This resistor has a resistance of one hundred ohms.
An ohm is the unit of electrical resistance.
These headphones are rated at thirty-two ohms.
Use a multimeter to measure the ohms.
She fell into a deep trance during the hypnosis.
The music put the dancers into a kind of trance.
The DJ played two hours of trance at the club.
He stared at the screen as if in a trance.
trance.note: Also a music style: "The DJ played trance all night."

ex: The gameplay is fun and easy to learn.
Fans love the fast gameplay of this game.
He streams his gameplay online every evening.
The graphics are great, but the gameplay is boring.

showbiz.note: Informal; the full form is "show business."

shutdown.note: Also any closing of a factory or system: "a computer shutdown."

ex: He wore a warm beanie in the snow.
She knitted a red beanie for her son.
Put on your beanie because it's cold outside.
My beanie fell off on the ski lift.

underground.note: Most often "underground" means below the ground: "an underground parking garage."

mandarin.note: Also called a "tangerine." Capital "Mandarin" is a Chinese language.
